## Authorization chain for `us.amazon.nova-micro-v1:0`

Bedrock cross-region (geographic/system-defined) inference profiles aren't a single resource check — the request is authorized against **two separate ARN types**, and your IAM policy has to cover both.

**Hop 1 — Inference profile ARN (source region)**
```
arn:aws:bedrock:<source-region>:<account-id>:inference-profile/us.amazon.nova-micro-v1:0
```
This is the one you already have `bedrock:InvokeModel` on. Passing this hop alone is not sufficient.

**Hop 2 — Underlying foundation-model ARNs (every destination region the profile fans out to)**
```
arn:aws:bedrock:<region-1>::foundation-model/amazon.nova-micro-v1:0
arn:aws:bedrock:<region-2>::foundation-model/amazon.nova-micro-v1:0
arn:aws:bedrock:<region-3>::foundation-model/amazon.nova-micro-v1:0
```
Bedrock resolves the profile to one of its underlying regional foundation-model resources at invocation time, and **evaluates `bedrock:InvokeModel` against that resolved foundation-model ARN too** — not just the profile ARN. If your policy's `Resource` block only lists the inference-profile ARN, the second check fails and you get `AccessDeniedException`, even though the profile ARN statement looks completely correct.

## Structured diagnosis

| Hop | Resource checked | Likely state in your case |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Inference profile | `inference-profile/us.amazon.nova-micro-v1:0` | ✅ Granted — matches what you confirmed |
| 2. Foundation model (per destination region) | `foundation-model/amazon.nova-micro-v1:0` in each region the `us.` profile spans | ❌ Likely missing — this is the typical root cause |
| 3. (If scoped tighter) Condition key binding | `bedrock:InferenceProfileArn` condition on the foundation-model statement | Only relevant if you're using a conditional grant pattern |

**Root cause:** your policy almost certainly grants `InvokeModel` on the inference-profile ARN only. Bedrock also requires an explicit `InvokeModel` grant on the plain foundation-model ARN(s) in **every region the profile can route to** — this is documented as a hard Bedrock requirement for cross-region inference, not an IAM quirk.

**Fix:** add a second statement granting `bedrock:InvokeModel` on `arn:aws:bedrock:<region>::foundation-model/amazon.nova-micro-v1:0` for each region in the `us.` profile's region set (check "Supported Regions and models for inference profiles" for the exact list this profile spans). Optionally tighten it with a `bedrock:InferenceProfileArn` condition so the foundation-model grant only applies when invoked via this specific profile.

If you want, I can look up exactly which regions the `us.amazon.nova-micro-v1:0` profile spans so you can scope the foundation-model statement precisely rather than guessing the region list.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
